name: AudioHub 0.2.0
body:
Reliability and security release, after an external code review. Recommended for everyone on 0.1.0.

**Security**
- The Chromecast audio stream is now served only to the speaker it was sent to, on a random per-route URL; it used to be reachable by any device on the local network.
- Incoming Cast frames are limited to 64 KiB.

**Audio quality**
- Lost AirPlay packets are now retransmitted on request, so busy Wi-Fi no longer causes gaps.
- The audio thread no longer waits on locks: a lock-free ring buffer sits between capture and the network senders.
- Moving the stereo-pair offset slider no longer clicks (30 ms crossfade).

**Fixes**
- AirPlay: a socket could be closed twice, which in rare cases closed an unrelated connection.
- AirPlay: after one timed-out request the RTSP control connection could break; responses are now matched to requests by sequence number.

**Tests**
- `audiohub selftest`: 55 automated checks, including a real Chromecast request recorded as a fixture. Also run under ThreadSanitizer. See TESTING.md.

**Install from the zip:**
 unzip, move AudioHub.app to Applications, right-click → Open (the app is not notarized). Allow it under System Settings → Privacy & Security → Screen & System Audio Recording → System Audio Recording Only, and allow local network access when asked.
Building from source with `scripts/install.sh` is recommended: with a local signing certificate (`scripts/make-signing-cert.sh`) the permissions survive updates.
